title: A Orbit for the Signal Again
premise: Tamsin Delacroix investigates impossible accidents for an insurance consortium that has quietly written off the colony world of Vesperine, and his field recordings become the only honest account of its slow, subsidized death. When gravity flickers across the entire system for nine seconds, he discovers the flicker was a weapon test disguised as an accident — and that the lie he must now keep alive is the fabricated insurance report holding two rival fleets from open war over Vesperine's reactor. As the reactor counts down to a breach that will make the lie permanent, Tamsin chooses truth over survival, broadcasting his recordings and shattering the truce in time to force both fleets into a joint evacuation. The book ends with Vesperine burning harmlessly into orbit while Tamsin, stripped of his career and half his memory of the woman who built the weapon, watches two former enemies share one rescue corridor.
about_author: Gideon Okafor is a former marine salvage auditor who spent six years documenting decommissioned orbital stations before turning to fiction. He writes near-future science fiction about paperwork, grief, and the machinery people build to avoid feeling either.

chapters.title: The Actuary of Small Disasters
chapters.summary: Tamsin Delacroix arrives on dying colony Vesperine to investigate a crane collapse no physics can explain. Through his POV we see the colony's quiet abandonment: rationed air, unpaid workers, a consortium that stopped answering messages years ago. Emotional beat: weary professionalism masking dread.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds
chapters.summary: Gravity fails across the entire system for exactly nine seconds; ships drift, children float, and Tamsin's recorder captures a harmonic pulse beneath the event. His POV, disoriented and awed. Emotional beat: the world tilts from routine investigation into something cosmic and wrong.

chapters.title: Claim Denied
chapters.summary: Back-channeling with his handler Odile, Tamsin learns the consortium pre-filed a claim against Vesperine before the flicker occurred. His POV, cold fear rising. Emotional beat: the realization that someone knew — and that his report is expected to say otherwise.

chapters.title: The Widow Who Counts Reactor Cycles
chapters.summary: Reactor engineer Sefa Okonkwo shows Tamsin her logs: containment cycles accelerating since the flicker. Her POV reveals she suspects the flicker was manufactured. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance between two people who trust only data.

chapters.title: Two Fleets at Anchor
chapters.summary: Above Vesperine, the corporate Concord fleet and the colonial Defense Ring sit in armed stalemate, each blaming the other for the gravity event. Alternating fleet-commander POVs. Emotional beat: mutual suspicion sharpening toward war.

chapters.title: A Lie Worth Two Fleets
chapters.summary: Odile orders Tamsin to file a report blaming Defense Ring sabotage — the fiction keeping the fleets talking instead of firing. His POV, morally cornered. Emotional beat: complicity settling on him like ballast.

chapters.title: What the Cranes Remembered
chapters.summary: Tamsin recovers the crane's black box: it was overridden remotely using Concord encryption older than the colony itself. His POV, forensic tension. Emotional beat: evidence in hand, and no safe place to put it.

chapters.title: Sefa's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Sefa calculates the reactor breaches in nineteen days if containment keeps cycling. Her POV interleaved with memories of her family evacuated years ago. Emotional beat: grief converted into stubborn precision.

chapters.title: The Man Who Sold Gravity
chapters.summary: Tamsin traces the flicker's signature to Dr. Ivo Renner, a disgraced gravitics researcher supposedly dead for a decade. His POV, obsessive pursuit. Emotional beat: the thrill of the hunt curdling into horror at what was sold.

chapters.title: Interrogation in Low Light
chapters.summary: Concord security detains Tamsin, probing what he knows; Odile quietly arranges his release by promising his silence. His POV, claustrophobic. Emotional beat: understanding he is now an asset, not an investigator.

chapters.title: The Recording Nobody Asked For
chapters.summary: Tamsin reviews all his field audio and finds the nine-second pulse repeated faintly in three earlier 'accidents' across the system. His POV, dawning scale. Emotional beat: loneliness of being the only witness to a pattern.

chapters.title: Renner, Alive and Unrepentant
chapters.summary: In a derelict station, Tamsin confronts Renner, who claims the flicker was a containment test gone wrong — and that stopping the next one requires hardware inside the reactor itself. Renner's POV briefly, then Tamsin's. Emotional beat: revulsion mixed with desperate pragmatism.

chapters.title: Skirmish at the Lagrange Line
chapters.summary: A Concord patrol and Defense Ring picket exchange fire after a navigation glitch echoes the gravity pulse. Dual commander POVs. Emotional beat: war arriving by accident, exactly as someone intended.

chapters.title: Odile's Confession
chapters.summary: Odile admits the consortium helped fund Renner to destabilize Vesperine and devalue it for buyout — and that Tamsin's false report is the linchpin of the peace. Her POV, guilt without remorse. Emotional beat: betrayal wearing the face of necessity.

chapters.title: Nineteen Days Become Six
chapters.summary: A second flicker accelerates the reactor's decay; Sefa revises the countdown to six days. Her POV, controlled panic. Emotional beat: time collapsing faster than anyone can lie.

chapters.title: The Choice Between Truths
chapters.summary: Tamsin holds two truths: exposing the conspiracy may trigger war before evacuation; keeping the lie condemns the colony to die unrecorded. His POV, interior crisis. Emotional beat: the price of survival made explicit.

chapters.title: Sabotage Aboard the Meridian
chapters.summary: Renner sabotages the Concord flagship's comms to prevent any joint evacuation order, forcing Tamsin to choose sides publicly. Action sequence, Tamsin's POV. Emotional beat: loyalty finally declared — to the colony, not the fleets.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: From the reactor control room, Tamsin transmits his full recordings — every accident, every log, Odile's confession — to both fleets simultaneously. His POV, terrified resolve. Emotional beat: the lie dies loudly, and the silence afterward is worse.

chapters.title: Countdown Under Guns
chapters.summary: Instead of war, both fleets freeze — then converge on Vesperine as Sefa's final containment window closes. Multi-POV chaos of an improvised joint evacuation under a failing sky. Emotional beat: enemies moving in sync out of sheer necessity.

chapters.title: What Renner Built
chapters.summary: Tamsin and Sefa enter the reactor core to disable Renner's resonance array; Renner dies ensuring it fires once more. Tamsin's POV, intimate and brutal. Emotional beat: sacrifice without redemption, the machine silenced at cost.

chapters.title: Corridor
chapters.summary: The reactor vents safely into orbit as forty thousand colonists crowd shared corridors of Concord and Ring ships. Tamsin, memory-scoured by proximity to the array, forgets the face of the woman who warned him first. His POV, hollowed tenderness. Emotional beat: survival purchased with pieces of himself.

chapters.title: An Orbit for the Signal Again
chapters.summary: Months later, Vesperine's burned hulk circles peacefully, transmitting Tamsin's recordings on loop as a navigational warning and a memorial. Both fleets co-sponsor the signal. His POV, quiet and diminished but free. Emotional beat: truth outliving the man who paid for it.
